purpose: Forensically classify every one of the 32 detailed-disposition disagreements (a strict superset of the 11 binary-credit disagreements) between Evaluation V2 and Phase 3F.1.5's independent second-pass adjudication, BEFORE designing any new taxonomy, protocol, sample, or rerun. This artifact is produced from the already-frozen Phase 3F.1.5 evidence (docs/evaluation-v2/08-second-pass-adjudication.json cross-joined with the sealed V2 labels) and changes nothing about it.

sourceData.note: Every binary-inclusive disagreement is a subset of the 32 detailed disagreements, as expected (a disposition-label difference large enough to flip the credit decision is necessarily also a disposition-label difference).

V2 granted PARTIAL credit to the compiled 'Acquisition' IR-definition against a GT claim about hard facility economics (commitment amounts, sublimits, maturity, availability period), reasoning 'core dimensions correspond ... silent on E_ECONOMICS.' The second pass, reading the same excerpt, finds no relationship between an M&A defined term and facility-sizing economics at all - not a partial match missing one dimension, but no correspondence on ANY dimension. The IDENTICAL candidate and near-identical v2Reason boilerplate also appear on two other, unrelated Section-1.01 definitional claims in this same sample (see net-income and permitted-supply-chain-financing below), which is the strongest evidence in this forensic pass that this is a genuine, repeatable defect in V2's own signal-correspondence layer for definitional/economic-metric claims, not a one-off GT or excerpt problem.

V2's two candidate clusters scored within 0.001 of each other (0.736 vs 0.735) and it declared AMBIGUOUS rather than force a winner. The second pass, reading the same two candidates, found one cluster clearly and specifically tracks the claim's trigger and effect and credited it outright. This is a genuine methodological question about where V2's near-tie ambiguity threshold should sit, not a false-credit risk (materiality is INFORMATIONAL) - flagged for future threshold review, not resolved here.

perCaseClassification.criticalFinding: THIS GT UNIT IS ONE OF THE 14 PHASE 3F.1.1 CONFIRMED FALSE CREDITS (see tests/fixtures/unseen-packages/phase-3f1-1-forensics/phase-3f1-1-scorer-bridge.json adversarialAudit.falseCreditSuspectIds). V2 correctly withholds credit here because the only semantically-corresponding candidates are DISCOVERY_CANDIDATE / INVENTORY_ONLY, never compiled. The second-pass reviewer, given only a natural-language 'does this substantively represent the claim' instruction and with NO knowledge of this unit's false-credit history (per the phase's own blinding rule), read the discovery candidate's correct-sounding excerpt and CREDITED it - independently reproducing the exact false-credit pattern this entire evaluation methodology exists to prevent. This is the single most important data point in this forensic pass: it is direct, concrete evidence that V2's stricter accountingRole gate is not over-cautious noise but is catching a real, previously-confirmed failure mode that a competent, careful, blinded human-equivalent reviewer will reproduce if not told about it.

perCaseClassification.status: LEAST_EXPLAINED_RESIDUAL_DISAGREEMENT - carried forward from Phase 3F.1.5, still unresolved
perCaseClassification.explanation: V2 credits compiled IR rule ir-rule:8543f9e7e76785c96a99e512 as an exact match. The second pass, reading the SAME packet, describes 'the two compiled IR rules in the packet' as 'Section 1.07 subordination-designation obligations' - i.e. it reads the candidate's own excerpt as being about a different subject than the guaranty claim entirely. The identical candidate ID (ir-rule:8543f9e7...) is also the second member of the EXACT_COMPOSITE match V2 grants for 10.06-reinstatement below, where the second pass again describes it as subordination-related. Two independent possibilities remain open and neither is resolved by this forensic pass alone: (a) V2's correspondence layer is matching this candidate to multiple, topically-adjacent-but-distinct Article X guaranty-mechanics claims on a shared signal that is not true semantic correspondence (a V2_LOGIC_DEFECT), or (b) the candidate's own excerpt genuinely spans both subordination and guaranty/reinstatement content (Article X guaranty provisions frequently bundle these) and the second-pass reviewer's characterization is incomplete (a SECOND_PASS_ERROR or CANDIDATE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE). Direct, excerpt-level examination of ir-rule:8543f9e7e76785c96a99e512's actual text is required to adjudicate between these - explicitly NOT performed in this phase, since doing so after seeing the disagreement result and then feeding a conclusion back into V2's disposition would itself be a prohibited post-hoc rewrite. This is flagged for direct, excerpt-level follow-up in a future iteration, not resolved now.

The second pass again characterizes both as Section 1.07 subordination obligations. Notably, for 10.04-defenses-waived the second pass credits ir-rule:fb5206d4... as genuinely representing 'election of remedies / no prior action' content - a THIRD characterization of the same candidate ID across three cases (subordination in 10.06, subordination in 10.01a's neighbour, election-of-remedies in 10.04). This internal inconsistency in how the same candidate is characterized across the second pass's own case narratives is itself evidence that something about the candidate's identity, excerpt assembly, or content is not being read consistently by at least one side - the single strongest concrete lead for future investigation, together with 10.01a-us-guaranty above.

STATE_TAXONOMY_MISMATCH.creditImpact: NONE - all 21 are binary-credit agreements; this cause explains the poor 37.3% detailed-agreement score far more than it reflects any evaluator disagreement about which candidates should be credited.

DISCOVERY_VS_REPRESENTATION_CONFUSION.creditImpact: ALL 6 are binary-credit disagreements; this is the largest genuine (credit-affecting) disagreement cluster, and includes the single most important finding in this forensic pass (doc-a::VI::6.10-chapeau reproducing a confirmed historical false credit).

V2_LOGIC_DEFECT.creditImpact: ALL 3 are binary-credit disagreements, all three instances of the SAME underlying defect (one over-broad definitional candidate credited against three unrelated Section-1.01 claims). This is a genuine residual defect in V2 itself, correctly caught by the second-pass gate, and is the single most actionable finding for a future V2 code change.

OTHER.creditImpact: Both are binary-credit disagreements (the two previously-flagged least-explained cases, 10.01a-us-guaranty and 10.06-reinstatement), both showing signs of a possible candidate-identity/consistency issue rather than a pure design-philosophy gap.

SEMANTIC_CORRESPONDENCE_DISAGREEMENT.creditImpact: One (2.21-returned-payments) is a binary-credit disagreement over a near-tie AMBIGUOUS threshold; one (10.04-defenses-waived) is a binary-credit AGREEMENT with a detailed-label difference over match completeness.

paretoAnalysis.headlineConclusion: The dominant driver of Phase 3F.1.5's failed 37.3% detailed-agreement score is NOT a credit-direction disagreement at all: 21 of 32 detailed disagreements (65.6%) are cases where both V2 and the second pass reach the identical NO_CREDIT conclusion but use different disposition vocabulary for it (V2's HONESTLY_UNRESOLVED/AMBIGUOUS vs. the second pass's single UNREPRESENTED bucket), because the second-pass reviewer was never given an equivalent taxonomy. Of the 11 genuine binary-credit disagreements, 6 trace to V2's deliberate (but never-explained-to-the-reviewer) discovery-vs-compiled-representation design choice - one of which (doc-a::VI::6.10-chapeau) is direct evidence that this design choice is CORRECT, since the second pass's more lenient reading reproduces a previously-confirmed false credit. 3 trace to a genuine, newly-discovered, repeatable V2_LOGIC_DEFECT (an over-broad definitional-candidate match) that should be fixed in a future iteration but is NOT fixed here. 2 remain genuinely unresolved and require direct excerpt-level follow-up, not a taxonomy or protocol fix.

rewriteProhibitionCompliance: This classification was produced entirely from data already frozen at Phase 3F.1.5's completion (SHA 7304cd2). No V2 matching logic, second-pass judgment, or ground truth was altered while or after performing this classification. The V2_LOGIC_DEFECT found (the over-broad 'Acquisition' definition candidate) is documented, not patched, per the phase charter's explicit instruction.
